card.statement:
Let $m^{-1}(\Ga)\subset \bar{\Ga}$ for any $m\in \cM$, $S\subset \cM$ a $G$-invariant subset, $u\in U$, $f\in
\Gamma$.

- $u\in U(S)$ if and only if $f_{S}\cdot u=0$ for every $f\in\Gamma$.

- If $T=\supp u \setminus S$ then $f_{T}\cdot u\in
    U(S)$ for every $f\in\Gamma$.

- If $f_{S}=\su{i=1}{n}f_{i}\otimes g_{i}$, $[am]\in L*\cM$ then $f_{S}\cdot
    [am]=[(\su{i=1}{n} f_{i}g_{i}^{m}a)m]$ $=[\pru{s\in S }{}(f -
    f^{ms^{-1}})am]$.

- Let $S$ be a $G$-orbit and $T$ an $G$-invariant subset in $\cM$. The $\Ga$-bimodule homomorphism $P^{T}_{S}(=P^{T}_{S}(f)):U(T)\myto U(S)$, $u\mapsto f_{T\setminus S}\cdot u,f\in \Gamma$ is either zero or $\Ker P_{S}^{T}=U(T\setminus S)$ (both cases are possible, cf. <<ref:enum-f-S-kills-U-S>>).

- Let $S=S_{1}\sqcup\dots\sqcup S_{n}$ be the decomposition of $S$ in $G$-orbits and $P_{S_{i}}^{S}:U(S)\myto U(S_{i})$ for some $f_{i}\in \Gamma$, $i=1,\dots,n$ are defined in <<ref:enum-f-S-mult-components-homomorphism>> nonzero homomorphisms. Then the homomorphism

\begin{equation}
P^{S}:U(S)\myto\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}
U(S_{i}),\
P^{S}=(P_{S_{1}}^{S},\dots,P_{S_{n}}^{S}),
\end{equation}

is a monomorphism.

- The statements above hold, if $\Ga$ is a Harish-Chandra subalgebra in $U$.
card.label: Lemma 7

paper.title: Galois orders
paper.abstract: We introduce and develop a structure theory of a new class of noncommutative rings - Galois orders, that generalize classical orders in noncommutative rings. Galois orders realized as certain subrings of invariants in skew semigroup rings. This class of rings contains many classical objects, in particular the Generalized Weyl algebras, the universal enveloping algebra of the general linear Lie algebra and certain rings of invariant differential operators on algebraic varieties.
